summary: Wattle-eyes and batises. Chinspot Batis is the common dry-woodland bird, grey-capped and yellow-eyed, the male without rufous and the female with a rufous chin-spot. Cape Batis is the heavily marked forest bird, with rufous wing coverts and yellow eyes when not breeding. Black-throated Wattle-eye has a red eye-wattle. The female’s breast is all black and the male has only a narrow black band. Newman’s size line for the wattle-eye is unreadable, so no length is stored.
